title: Turning My Obsidian Vault Into a Local AI Engineer — Filip Makraduli, Superlinked
talk_summary: Filip Makraduli shows an MCP server that offloads document OCR, redaction, NER, and summarization from Claude Code to a self-hosted Superlinked/SIE inference cluster, cutting token spend and keeping sensitive data in a private VPC. The talk is mostly a product demo of SIE's GPU cluster, model hot-swapping, per-worker batching, and LoRA serving, with a few transferable architecture ideas about offloading cheap subtasks to a separate inference tier.

takeaways.technique: Offload deterministic preprocessing to a cheap sidecar model tier
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of feeding raw PDFs/scans/images into the main agent, an MCP tool runs OCR/redaction/NER on a separate inference cluster and returns compact markdown, so the main model only sees the distilled artifact.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you pre-process that with good open-source OCR models and then return to your main agent harness ... you get the context, but also benefit on the lower token spent

takeaways.technique: Route by model warmth/cache state, not just price
takeaways.what_they_do: They note that hitting an already-loaded ('hot') model can be cheaper end-to-end than reloading a cheaper cold model, and plan routing that accounts for what is currently resident.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it would be cheaper to hit a model that's already hot, but more expensive rather than reloading a model that's cheaper, but kind of not already there

takeaways.technique: Single MCP edge for all heavy subtasks
takeaways.what_they_do: They expose one MCP server with tools (docs-to-markdown, redact, extract entities, summarize, QA) so any harness calls the same interface for offloaded work rather than each agent reimplementing it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the same kind of MCP edge handles every document job, so you can do question answering, pulling facts, reading documents

takeaways.technique: Per-worker batching and right-sized worker pools
takeaways.what_they_do: They found a shared queue that workers pull from performed worse than batching per worker, and they size worker pools to task weight (L4 spot for light models, bigger GPUs for heavy).
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you kind of do the batching without having one shared queue that then each of the workers pull from, in our testing ... performance was lower

takeaways.technique: Eval models per task before routing to them
takeaways.what_they_do: They benchmark candidate models on task-specific evals (MTEB for embeddings) before trusting a router or judge, and warn about judges that get gamed or biased.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're also very strong on evals and trying to test models before doing this
takeaways.numbers: claims ~10x lower price with 99.8% of frontier embedding quality on MTEB

takeaways.technique: Watch thinking-token models on constrained outputs
takeaways.what_they_do: A summarization tool failed because a reasoning model put everything in thinking tokens, yielding empty or too-short output; they flag toggling thinking per task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the summarization was either very short or it didn't happen cuz everything was done on the thinking side
